newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran secures Indian fertiliser plant investment.
newsitem.headline: Iran secures Indian fertiliser plant investment.

text.p: Two Indian firms have finalised plans for a $400 million joint-venture fertiliser project in Iran's Qeshm island free zone, the London-based Middle East Economic Digest (MEED) weekly reported in its latest edition.

Indian Farmers Fertiliser Co-operative (IFFC) and Krishak Bharati Co-operative are taking a 60 percent in the plant at the trade zone to produce an annual 726,000 tonnes of urea for the Indian market.
Qeshm Free Authority (QFA) will hold 40 percent equity.
"Agreement follows more than two years of negotiations on the price of the gas to be used as feedstock to make ammonia-urea," MEED reported.
QFA had agreed a price of $0.75 a million British thermal units which would be fixed for five years.
An estimated 1.5 million cubic metres a day of gas would be supplied to plant from fields in the island and on the mainland near Bandar Abbas, the magazine reported.
